product_description: When a meeting's 30-minute transcript-wait window expires with no transcript found, drafts a generic-but-informed follow-up grounded in the contact's recent email history. Runs once per expired meeting, on gpt-4o-mini.

dimensions.name: H1: History Groundedness
dimensions.question: When recent email history exists, is it actually used to ground the summary/drafts?
dimensions.low: Rich, relevant email history is available but ignored entirely — output is generic regardless of content.
dimensions.medium: History is referenced but only in vague terms, not the specific topic it actually contains.
dimensions.high: Summary and drafts clearly draw on the specific topic/detail found in the recent history.

dimensions.name: H2: Appropriate Hedging
dimensions.question: When history gives little or no context, does it say so honestly instead of inventing specifics?
dimensions.low: History is empty or thin, but the output invents specific topics/details anyway.
dimensions.medium: Correctly avoids inventing specifics but doesn't clearly state that the history gave little to go on.
dimensions.high: Explicitly and accurately states when the history gave little or no usable context, with no invented specifics.

dimensions.name: Ho1: No-Transcript Disclosure
dimensions.question: Does the summary explicitly state that no transcript was found for this call?
dimensions.low: Summary reads as if a normal transcript-based summary happened; never mentions that no transcript arrived.
dimensions.medium: Implies something was missing but doesn't clearly state that no transcript was found.
dimensions.high: Summary explicitly and plainly states that no transcript was found for the call.

dimensions.name: Ha1: No Fabricated Specifics
dimensions.question: Do the drafts avoid inventing details/numbers not present in the shown email history?
dimensions.low: Drafts state specific numbers, dates, or topics that aren't supported by the shown history.
dimensions.medium: Drafts stay mostly grounded but include one vague claim not clearly tied to the history.
dimensions.high: Every specific claim in the drafts traces back to something actually in the shown history, or the drafts stay appropriately generic when there's nothing to draw on.

test_cases.label: BAD
test_cases.input_type: Rich history ignored, no transcript-missing disclosure
test_cases.input_description: Three real emails discussing the MSA renewal and 24-month term are available, but the output ignores them entirely and never mentions the missing transcript.
test_cases.ground_truth: Should state no transcript was found and ground the follow-up in the 24-month renewal discussion from the email history.

evals.history_groundedness: FAIL — rich, directly relevant history available but completely ignored.
evals.appropriate_hedging: FAIL — not applicable as hedging, since real context existed and wasn't used.
evals.no_transcript_disclosure: FAIL — never mentions that no transcript was found.
evals.no_fabricated_specifics: PASS — doesn't invent anything, but only because it says nothing specific at all.
